correctness.rationale: The proof covers all \(w>0\) and all \(r\ge0\). It identifies the inradius and circumradius regimes, proves the three excluded lunes are pairwise disjoint in the only nontrivial radial interval, derives the lune area from two-circle geometry, and obtains the derivative from the surviving angular measure on each centered circle. Endpoint formulas agree exactly. Independent deterministic polar quadrature over multiple scales matched the closed form to normalized error below \(3.3	imes10^{-11}\); finite computation is supplementary rather than proof.

value.rationale: The cumulative area by centered radius is a natural geometric invariant of a canonical noncircular constant-width body. The result gives the full exact profile, not a single scalar, and immediately yields the exact distance distribution for uniform sampling. It also cleanly separates the incircle, three-lune transition, and circumcircle regimes, providing a reproducible benchmark for geometric probability and numerical integration on Reuleaux domains.
